scope.population: The Manger and flanking Asses as described by Aratus
scope.assumptions: Visibility under a clear sky and asymmetric dimming of the two stars
scope.uncertainty: Apparent star changes are treated as weather omens, without evidence here of forecast accuracy
scope.quantifiers: Two flanking stars; directional qualitative forecast

support.quote:
On a sudden, when all the sky is clear, the Manger wholly disappears,
        while the stars that go on either side seem nearer drawn to one another: not slight then is the storm with which
        the fields are deluged. If the Manger darken and both stars remain unaltered, they herald rain. But if the Ass
        to the North of the Manger shine feebly through a faint mist, while the Southern Ass is gleaming bright, expect
        wind from the South: but if in turn the Southern Ass is cloudy and the Northern bright, watch for the North
        wind.

canonical_record.label: Aratus's seabird and shorebird wind signs
canonical_record.summary: Aratus describes a heron flying landward from the sea with cries, storm petrels turning toward winds, and ducks or gulls beating wings on shore as signs preceding gales.

assertions.statement: Aratus describes a heron flying landward from the sea with cries, storm petrels turning toward winds, and ducks or gulls beating wings on shore as signs preceding gales.

scope.population: Behavioral wind and gale signs in Phaenomena
scope.assumptions: Herons, storm petrels, wild ducks and gulls in the described conditions
scope.uncertainty: Ancient observational attribution; no controlled predictive test
scope.quantifiers: Several named bird types; qualitative gale forecasts

support.quote:
[913] When, too, the heron in disordered flight comes landward from he sea with many a scream, he is precursor
        of the gale at sea. Anon, too, the stormy petrels when the flit in calm, move in companies to face the coming
        winds. Oft before a gale the wild ducks or sea-wheeling gulls beat their wings on the shore, or a cloud is
        lengthwise resting on the mountain peaks.

canonical_record.label: Theophrastus's local mountain-cloud weather guidance
canonical_record.summary: Theophrastus says mountainous and coastal terrain affects cloud movements when winds change and advises attending to local conditions and knowledgeable local observers when interpreting weather signs.

assertions.statement: Theophrastus says mountainous and coastal terrain affects cloud movements when winds change and advises attending to local conditions and knowledgeable local observers when interpreting weather signs.

scope.population: Local weather signs in mountain-and-valley regions
scope.assumptions: Mountains, valleys, coastal terrain, wind shifts, locally informed observation
scope.uncertainty: Textual description and recommendation without a controlled prediction study
scope.quantifiers: Region-specific, with no universal forecast probability

support.quote:
Of the remaining signs some belong specially to all such lands as contain high mountains and valleys, specially where such mountains extend down to the sea: for, when the winds begin to blow, the clouds are thrown against such places, and, when the winds
p393
change, the clouds also change⁠
2
and take a contrary direction, and, as they become laden with moisture, they settle down in the hollows because of their weight. Wherefore good heed must be taken to the local conditions of the region in which one is placed. It is indeed always possible to find such an observer, and the signs learnt from such persons are the most trustworthy.

canonical_record.label: Theophrastus's red-sky rain time window
canonical_record.summary: Theophrastus describes a reddish sky before sunrise as a rain sign for the same day or within three days, and a red sunset sky as a similar but less certain sign.

assertions.statement: Theophrastus describes a reddish sky before sunrise as a rain sign for the same day or within three days, and a red sunset sky as a similar but less certain sign.

scope.population: Dawn and sunset color observations in the described weather lore
scope.assumptions: Reddish dawn versus red sky at sunset
scope.uncertainty: Claimed forecast interval and comparative certainty are textual, not empirically established probabilities
scope.quantifiers: Within three days or earlier; comparative certainty only

support.quote: Now the signs of rain appear to be as follows: most unmistakable is that which occurs at dawn, when the sky has a reddish appearance before sunrise; for this usually indicates rain within three days, if not on that very day. Other signs point the same way: thus a red sky at sunset indicates rain within three days, if not before, though less certainly than a red sky at dawn.

canonical_record.label: Theophrastus's ant-egg movement omens
canonical_record.summary: Theophrastus treats ants moving their eggs from hollow anthills to higher ground as a sign of rain and moving them down as a sign of fair weather.

assertions.statement: Theophrastus treats ants moving their eggs from hollow anthills to higher ground as a sign of rain and moving them down as a sign of fair weather.

scope.population: Ants' egg transport as an attributed sign of weather
scope.assumptions: Movement up from a hollow place versus downward
scope.uncertainty: Historical forecast claim without verified prediction accuracy
scope.quantifiers: Two movement directions; qualitative rain/fair outcome

support.quote:
It is a sign of rain if ants⁠
38
in a hollow place carry their eggs up from the ant-hill to the high ground, a sign of fair weather if they carry them down.
